subject: physics
topicTitle: NEB Class 11 Physics — Potential and Potential Energy — 2024
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define electric potential at a point. State its SI unit and the relation between electric field and potential.
questions.solution:
**Electric potential** is the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to the point (W/q₀). SI unit: **volt (V) = J/C**.

Field and potential are linked by **E = −dV/dr** — the field points down the steepest potential slope.
questions.knowledgeNote: Potential is a scalar (no direction) while field is a vector — potential problems need half the bookkeeping.

questions.question: Calculate the electric potential at 0.5 m from a point charge of 2 μC in air.
questions.knowledgeNote: V ∝ 1/r but E ∝ 1/r² — at large distances the potential outlives the field.

questions.question: What are equipotential surfaces? Write any three of their properties.
questions.solution:
Surfaces (real or imaginary) over which the potential is constant everywhere.

(1) No work is done moving a charge along one. (2) Field lines always cross them at right angles. (3) Two equipotential surfaces never intersect (that would give one point two potentials).
questions.knowledgeNote: For a point charge they are concentric spheres; for a uniform field, parallel planes.

questions.question: Define the electron-volt. Convert 1 eV into joules.
questions.solution:
**1 eV** is the kinetic energy an electron gains crossing a 1 V potential difference.

1 eV = e × 1 V = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)(1) = **1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Atomic energies live in eV, nuclear in MeV — converting to joules first is the safe route in combined problems.

questions.question: Two charges +3 μC and −2 μC are placed 0.3 m apart in air. Calculate the electric potential energy of the system.
questions.solution:
U = kq₁q₂/r = (9 × 10⁹)(3 × 10⁻⁶)(−2 × 10⁻⁶)/0.3

U = −54 × 10⁻³/0.3 = **−0.18 J**.

The negative sign means work must be done to separate them — opposite charges bind the system.
questions.knowledgeNote: Like charges give positive U (work stored pushing them together); unlike charges give negative U (bound).

questions.question: Show that the electric potential everywhere inside a uniformly charged hollow sphere equals its surface value.
questions.solution:
Inside the shell E = 0 (Gauss's law — no enclosed charge). Since E = −dV/dr, zero field means dV/dr = 0: V is constant throughout the interior.

At the surface r = R it must join the outside value Q/(4πε₀R), so **V = Q/(4πε₀R) everywhere inside**, right up to the centre.
questions.knowledgeNote: Constant potential ≠ zero potential — the interior sits at the full surface voltage, which is why a hollow conductor is still dangerous to touch.
